units.passage: Although there are opportunities for the appropriate use of AI generative tools, students should not use these tools to generate reflections for writing assignments (e.g., journals, reflective essays).

units.passage: There has been growing concern about the use of Chrome extensions to complete online assignments and assessments. We have seen an uptick in students using AI to answer assignment questions, either by copying/pasting questions into AI (such as ChatGPT) or by having an AI browser extension answer the question for them.
units.why: "We have seen an uptick in students using AI to answer assignment questions, either by copying/pasting questions into AI... or by having an AI browser extension answer the question for them" describes misuse of AI to produce the answers students submit; informs, general, P19.
units.fit_note: Describes the misuse of copying questions into AI or using an AI browser extension; it states no explicit rule. Coder B placed it under P20 (feeding questions to AI); P19 was kept because the sentence is about AI answering the questions for the student. Describes a concern about the behavior; no explicit prohibition is stated.

units.passage: Do not use generative AI tools or features to create, solve, summarize, translate, revise, or substantially transform work submitted for credit.

units.fit_note: Also bars summarizing, translating and revising. / Also bars revising and translating, which overlaps with P21 and P18.

units.why: Not permitted: AI-generated sentences in final work "without quotation marks and attribution"; AI producing submitted text, P19, here barred only when unattributed.
units.fit_note: Prohibition applies only when unattributed. The ban applies to unattributed generated text; quoted and attributed text is not banned.

units.passage: Using AI to write arguments, code, proofs, or problem solutions that you submit as your own
units.why: Not permitted: "Using AI to write arguments, code, proofs, or problem solutions that you submit as your own", P19.

units.passage: Examples of unacceptable use of AI in PSY 32: asking ChatGPT to answer your assignment questions or outline a project proposal.
units.why: Unacceptable: "asking ChatGPT to answer your assignment questions or outline a project proposal", AI producing the submitted work, P19.

units.passage: Copying or closely paraphrasing AI-generated text/code/solutions as part of your submission without clear acknowledgment and substantive original contribution.

units.fit_note: Prohibited only without acknowledgment and original contribution. Allowed with clear acknowledgment and substantive original contribution.

units.passage: There is one exception: you are welcome to use AI tools for pre-submission editing (spell-check and grammar-check) as long as you do not use them for thinking or drafting.
units.why: 'as long as you do not use them for thinking or drafting' limits the editing exception: AI may not do the thinking or drafting (P19).
units.fit_note: Bans thinking and drafting with AI rather than generating the submitted text specifically.

units.passage: However, its use is expressly forbidden for writing database-related code, including SQL queries, stored procedures, and triggers.
units.why: "its use is expressly forbidden for writing database-related code, including SQL queries" forbids AI-written code in the core topic, P19.

units.passage: Using an LLM to summarize a paper to get a high-level idea about its content can be helpful, for example, in deciding whether to read it., but copy-pasting that summary as a concluding paragraph for a paper you have written could be problematic.
units.why: "copy-pasting that summary as a concluding paragraph for a paper you have written could be problematic" cautions against pasting AI text into your work, P19, should-not.

units.why: 'AI must not be used to generate full sections of your presentation's content or your abstract' bans AI producing submitted content, P19.

units.why: 'prohibited uses (e.g. submitting AI-generated text as one's own work)' gives the example prohibited use, so P19.

units.passage: Students should not have another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them, which includes hiring a person or a company to write assignments and using artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT.
